title: CodexBar: choose the dashboard's visual world
question: The dice picked Dark Cockpit. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All data shown is made up for illustration.

options.label: Dark Cockpit
options.lineage: Airliner glass cockpits (EICAS engine displays, MFD pages) and their dark-cockpit rule
options.thesis: Every quota is a gauge in a dark cockpit: it stays silent while the reading is normal, and caution or warning lights only come on as a limit closes in.
materials: vertical tape gauges with limit ticks
options.viewport: A borderless window with a thin annunciator strip at the top that lights only for amber/red accounts. Below it, a grid of Chart-page cards, each built as an instrument: tape gauges with the reset countdown in cyan, a one-line takeaway, and a caption. Soft-key tabs switch the dashboard pages (Usage, Spend, History).
options.risk: Turns into cosplay if the bezel, fonts or chrome get too literal; it has to stay a calm Windows tool.

raised.raise: Cards snap to a visible cell grid, and the grid hairlines are part of the instrument panel.
Every gauge and chart uses the same fixed scale, so accounts can be compared honestly at a glance.
The focused account is drawn brightest and the rest dim back, like the chosen line on a transit map.
Capacity is a fixed physical length, and reset times are right-aligned tabular figures pressed against the margin.

options.label: Editor-Native
options.lineage: Zed, Linear and Raycast: dense, keyboard-first power tools
options.thesis: The dashboard reads like a pane of the editor you already live in: dense, quiet and keyboard-first.
options.viewport: A left rail with the dashboard views and a Ctrl+K command bar. The main pane holds a dense account table sorted by urgency, with inline sparklines. Chart-page cards for the focused account sit below.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most dev-tool dashboards land, and it stands out only through craft.

options.label: Departures Board
options.thesis: Resets are departures: every account is a row ranked by time-to-reset, and a refresh clatters through the board.
options.viewport: A full-width board: provider, account, limit, used %, and the reset time in flap cells. Amber lamps mark caution and red rows mark blocked. Chart-page cards open beneath the selected row.
options.case: Fuses cleanly, since resets map to ranked departures; it is weaker at charts and money than the cockpit.
options.risk: Becomes a novelty if every view is a board; charts need their own register.

options.label: Monochrome Precision
options.lineage: Vercel/Geist restraint: one neutral scale and an accent that means something
options.thesis: Almost no color: the one account about to block you is the only thing on screen that gets any.
options.viewport: Chart-page cards in a strict grid, all grayscale. The single most urgent card carries the accent and reads first; the rest stay quiet.
options.case: Developers already know this look, but it ranks urgency less clearly than the cockpit's caution system.
options.risk: Restraint done timidly reads as generic.

options.label: Crouwel Grid
options.thesis: Numbers built on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Huge percentage numerals built from grid cells.
options.case: Developers don't recognize themselves in a type poster, and monumental numerals hide the ranking.
options.risk: Becomes a poster, not a tool.
options.kept: The visible cell grid that cards snap to.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: Botanical plates at a fixed scale
options.thesis: A quota's lifecycle shown as fixed-scale plates.
options.viewport: History as a row of same-scale plates.
options.case: Off-world for developers and unclear about urgency.
options.kept: One fixed scale across every chart, so comparisons are honest.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Each limit is a tape side that must not overflow.
options.case: Too nostalgic for a daily tool, and hard to scan for urgency.
options.kept: Capacity as a hard fixed length, with times right-aligned tight.

options.label: Midnight Transit Map
options.thesis: Providers as colored lines and accounts as stations.
options.case: The map metaphor adds a translation step between the reader and the numbers.
options.kept: The chosen line burns brightest while the rest recede.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The gpui-kit Chart page played straight: a sidebar plus a grid of white chart cards with blue bars, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A sidebar of dashboard views, with Chart-page cards (title, period, chart, takeaway, caption) in a 3-4 column grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any analytics dashboard by design.
